div.div:
Minikube driver decides what the node is
Docker / Podman: node is a container
KVM / VirtualBox / Hyper-V: node is a VM
none: Kubernetes runs directly on the Linux host

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div:
Optional multi-node mode
minikube start --nodes=3
Minikube can create additional worker nodes, but the normal/default learning setup is a single node containing both control-plane and workloads.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1218px; height: 1px; padding-top: 936px; margin-left: 187px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Key difference from kind: kind is primarily designed around Kubernetes nodes as containers. Minikube is a local Kubernetes environment with selectable drivers; Docker is only one possible driver. With the Docker driver, Docker creates the Minikube node container, while kubelet uses containerd inside that node to run Kubernetes Pod containers.
